notes: Measured on AE 2026 8 bpc: 'Gaussian Blur (Legacy)' (ADBE Gaussian Blur) is NOT a Gaussian: its renders at Blurriness 10 and 25 are pixel-identical (0 difference over the whole frame) to Fast Blur (Legacy) (ADBE Fast Blur) with Repeat Edge Pixels OFF, and an independent fit confirms it (edge step-response kurtosis 2.60 = three boxes; best 3-box radius rho = 0.370 * Blurriness at both settings, vs 0.369 for fast_blur_legacy). Model: per axis, THREE iterated box blurs of the PREMULTIPLIED colour, each of fractional radius rho = 0.369 * Blurriness (weight 1 on |x| <= floor(rho), frac(rho) at floor(rho)+1), horizontal then vertical, on an unbounded transparent plane (no Repeat Edge Pixels option in this effect). The shader is ae_fast_blur_legacy.wgsl with repeatEdge forced off (exact b*b*b composite kernel per axis, one RGBA8 rounding per axis instead of AE's per-box rounding: <= 2 LSB). Large blurs: direct taps up to Blurriness ~130, exact bilinear pairs up to ~265, then a strided coarse kernel (approximation). Blur Dimensions 2/3 (Horizontal/Vertical only) are not covered by the refs (inherited from fast_blur_legacy, checked there against the numpy model). AE grows the layer by the blur: give the node a pad >= 3*(floor(0.369*Blurriness)+1) px when the content reaches the layer edge. Not reproduced: Compositing Options (AE 3).
